claims.text: The plan of 4 October was a real identity for every agent and every user: a Google Workspace account of its own, provisioned by RiskMandate, with a mailbox, a calendar, a drive and a login.
claims.quote: a Google Workspace account of its own, provisioned by us, with a mailbox, a calendar, a drive and a login

claims.text: The owner's agents each have a Workspace mailbox, a Claude seat and a GitHub account, at about seven pounds a month per agent.
claims.quote: It also costs about seven pounds a month per agent, which is nothing

claims.text: The account is the blast radius, and an agent whose account is empty on day one can leak nothing on day one.
claims.quote: The account is the blast radius, and an agent whose account is empty on day one can leak nothing on day one.

claims.text: Standard Workspace storage has no admin-proof zone: a super administrator can reach any user's Drive, and client-side encryption is only on the top editions, so encryption had to happen in sgit before Google.
claims.quote: standard Workspace storage has no admin-proof zone

claims.text: The Google Cloud terms, last modified 2 September 2026, say the customer will not sell, resell, sublicense, transfer or distribute any of the Services.
claims.quote: sell, resell, sublicense, transfer, or distribute any or all of the Services.

claims.text: The acceptable use policy forbids End User Accounts assigned to business functions rather than to human beings for the purpose of sharing files, which ended the agent as a seat.
claims.quote: to create End User Accounts assigned to business functions rather than to human beings for the purpose of sharing files within or outside of the domain

claims.text: The policy also forbids reselling End User Accounts as added into a commercial product offered to third parties, which ended the shared tier as designed.
claims.quote: to resell End User Accounts, or parts thereof, as added into a commercial product offered to third parties.

claims.text: The design pack now says a Workspace tenant may only hold one organisation's people unless Google agrees otherwise in writing, and data sensitivity does not change this.
claims.quote: A Workspace tenant may only hold one organisation's people, unless Google agrees otherwise in writing. Data sensitivity does not change this.

claims.text: One correction to the pack: the substitute or similar service clause it cites as section 2.6 is in the legacy free-edition agreement, not the current Cloud terms, so that worry is retired.
claims.quote: It is not in the current Cloud terms. The worry can be retired; the resale and function-account findings cannot.

claims.text: Of five options, the second won the shared tier and the MVP: one cloud project per deployment, Google's Identity Platform for login and a bucket of ciphertext, with no mailbox.
claims.quote: The second row won the shared tier and the MVP.

claims.text: Google's Identity Platform costs nothing to fifty thousand monthly active users and a fraction of a cent after; Amazon's Cognito is free to ten thousand.
claims.quote: costs nothing to fifty thousand monthly active users and a fraction of a cent after

value.unit: monthly active users free on Identity Platform

claims.text: Every identity provider looked at has an administrator who can become any user: Cognito sets passwords, Firebase mints custom tokens, a key service decrypts for any principal with permission.
claims.quote: Every identity provider we looked at has an administrator who can become any user.

claims.text: Login decides which paths you may touch and the passkey decides whether the bytes mean anything; an administrator can fake the first and never the second.
claims.quote: Login decides which paths you may touch. The passkey decides whether the bytes mean anything. An administrator can fake the first and never the second.

claims.text: The one place the rule does not hold is the code: whoever controls the repository or the DNS controls the app and every user who loads it.
claims.quote: Whoever controls the repository or the DNS controls the app and every user who loads it.

claims.text: The passkey is scoped to exactly one subdomain and never the apex, because a passkey scoped to the apex could be asserted by any of the twenty-seven sibling sites.
claims.quote: a passkey scoped to the apex could be asserted by any of the twenty-seven sibling sites

claims.text: sgit refuses to be a secrets manager; the partnership call of 24 September asked a partner to provide one, and no partner stepped forward in eleven days.
claims.quote: No partner stepped forward in eleven days, which is not a complaint

value.unit: days without a partner stepping forward

claims.text: The keyring is one encrypted file per user, in a bucket only that user's login can reach, holding their key pair and every small secret under a key derived from the passkey's PRF output.
claims.quote: The keyring is one encrypted file per user in a bucket only that user's login can reach.

claims.text: A recovery code of 128 bits, shown once, is the second way in; lose every passkey and the code and the data is gone, and the terms say so.
claims.quote: A recovery code of 128 bits, shown once, is the second way in.

claims.text: The keyring uses the algorithms sgit pki already uses, RSA-OAEP at 4096 bits and ECDSA P-256, so an envelope sealed in the browser is one the command line can open.
claims.quote: RSA-OAEP at 4096 bits and ECDSA P-256, so that an envelope sealed in the browser is one the command line can open

claims.text: The WebAuthn Level 3 specification that defines the PRF extension became a W3C Recommendation on 25 August 2026; Chrome, Edge, Safari 18 and Firefox ship it.
claims.quote: became a W3C Recommendation on 25 August 2026

claims.text: Bitwarden shipped vault unlock by passkey on the PRF extension in November 2025, and Dashlane with Yubico a month earlier, both with caveats about platforms and authenticators.
claims.quote: Bitwarden shipped vault unlock by passkey on the same extension in November 2025, and Dashlane with Yubico a month earlier

claims.text: The first thing built is a password manager, because it contains every risky piece of the design in one small, testable product.
claims.quote: The first thing built is a password manager, not because the world needs another one but because it contains every risky piece of the design in one small, testable product

claims.text: The acceptance test is written into the brief: hand an owner of the project a user id, ask them to produce one plaintext field, and publish the write-up of the attempt.
claims.quote: hand an owner of the project a user id and ask them to produce one plaintext field, then publish the write-up of the attempt

claims.text: An agent has a service identity, not a seat; it gets a lane for signed mail where the site is the identity, and a read key released from a person's keyring, scoped and time-limited.
claims.quote: An agent has a service identity, not a seat.

claims.text: Microsoft's Entra Agent ID, Okta's agent product, Google Cloud's Agent Identity and Anthropic's managed agents are all workload identity: they prove which agent called, not who holds the user's key.
claims.quote: All of these are workload identity: good for proving which agent called, useless for the question this article is about, which is who holds the user's key.

claims.text: Every project needs to log people in, keep sensitive data nobody else can read, and give agents an identity; each has good products and none is all three.
claims.quote: Each of those has good products. None of them is all three, and the research found nothing on the shelf that is.

claims.text: The nearest things to a login product with per-user zero-knowledge storage are two small open-source projects, Userbase and Etebase, both password-derived and neither doing agents.
claims.quote: both password-derived rather than passkey-based, neither of which does agents

claims.text: GDPR Article 34 lifts the duty to tell individuals about a breach where data was rendered unintelligible to anyone not authorised, such as by encryption, if the key's confidentiality is intact.
claims.quote: unintelligible to any person who is not authorised to access it, such as encryption

claims.text: Unless the owner is missing something obvious, there should be a much simpler way to do this than there is, which is why the design pack is published to be corrected.
claims.quote: unless I am missing something obvious, which is a real possibility and the reason this is published rather than kept

claims.text: None of the MVP exists yet: the repository holds a README and a licence, and the nine releases in the build order will each appear in the site's reality file before being described in the present tense.
claims.quote: The repository holds a README and a licence.

claims.text: This is a startup's account of a week, not a survey, and the question at the end is a real one; the terms figure is marked not legal advice.
claims.quote: It is a startup's account of a week, not a survey, and the question at the end is a real one.

claims.text: The distributors' account of Google's direct-partner requirements, a hundred seats, a business plan and a credit check, could not be verified against a Google page.
claims.quote: that is their account, not Google's, and I have not been able to verify it against a Google page

claims.text: The one-page infographic was generated with ChatGPT from the published text; its closing line is the other model's condensation of the ending, not a sentence from the article.
claims.quote: the closing line in the picture's last panel is credited to the article but is the other model's condensation of its ending, not a sentence from it

claims.text: Five design documents and a starter prompt were written on 4 and 5 October 2026 and published as the identity and secrets design pack.
claims.quote: Five design documents and a starter prompt written on 4 and 5 October 2026
